title: Products and research
purpose: When I am about to bet money on a new product, a category or next year's plan, open Market research to know if the market is growing, where we are falling behind it, what costs and buyers are doing, and which new product is worth funding.
fires: The yearly plan made on gut feel, the consultant's market report, late-night scrolling in spy tools, the supplier's "this is selling like crazy" pitch, and the habit of never looking at the market at all.
not_for: A reseller who tests a new trending product every week for quick cash; they need a fast product hunt, not a read on the market.

jobs.job: When I am about to put $20k or more into a first stock order for a new product, tell me if it makes money after every real cost and has demand from more than one source, so I do not sink cash into a product that will not sell
jobs.circumstance: Supplier quote in hand, samples approved, a deposit due in 10 days, and a partner asking "are we sure?"

progress.functional: know margin per unit after landed cost, fees, returns and ad cost per sale, and whether demand shows in 2 or more places
progress.emotional: stop the sleepless nights before a big stock bet
progress.social: show my partner or investor a go or no-go with the numbers behind it

jobs.hire_today: a spreadsheet I build at night, a freelancer's research, or gut feel and the supplier's word
jobs.fire: the one-off spreadsheet and the gut call

forces.push: one bad stock order can eat a quarter's profit and cash
forces.pull: a single go or no-go with each cost and each demand source shown
forces.habit: I have picked winners by feel before
forces.anxiety: what if the model misses a cost, like returns or duties, and the margin is not real

jobs.little_hire: before every new product and every big first reorder

watch.metric: modelled margin per unit after all costs and ad cost per sale, against the owner's floor
watch.source: supplier quote, fees and ad costs in the brand brain

drives.metric: gross profit from products launched in the last 12 months

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 of the last 5 launches lost money after ad costs. After: a no-go stops 1 of them before the deposit, saving about $25k.
jobs.not_for: a brand that only restocks its existing range and launches nothing new

jobs.job: When a supplier sends a new quote or freight rates move, tell me whether my input costs are rising or falling across my top products, so I act before margin shrinks
jobs.circumstance: A price-rise letter from the supplier, freight up 30 percent, and the next reorder due in 6 weeks

progress.functional: know landed cost per unit for the top 10 products, quarter against quarter
progress.emotional: stop being surprised by thin margin at month end
progress.social: negotiate with the supplier from facts

jobs.hire_today: the bookkeeper's cost of goods at year end, or a sheet updated at reorder time
jobs.fire: finding out after the stock arrives

forces.push: a 10 percent cost rise can wipe out a third of profit
forces.pull: cost per unit by product, with what drove each change
forces.habit: I accept the new price and move on
forces.anxiety: what if the cost view misses freight, duties or packaging

jobs.little_hire: every reorder and every quarter

watch.metric: landed cost per unit, top 10 products, quarter against quarter
watch.source: supplier invoices and freight bills in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: landed cost rose 14 percent over 2 quarters and was found at year end. After: it is seen at the next quote, and price and supplier choices are made in time.
jobs.not_for: a print-on-demand store where the supplier's price is the only cost and changes rarely

jobs.job: When a tariff, duty or trade rule change is announced, tell me which of my products it hits and by how much per unit, so I reprice, reroute or reorder before it lands
jobs.circumstance: A news headline about new tariffs, 6 products made in the country named, and stock orders already at sea

progress.functional: know the added cost per unit and the date it starts, for each product
progress.emotional: stop the panic from headlines I cannot size
progress.social: give the team and supplier a clear plan

jobs.hire_today: a customs broker's email, the freight forwarder, or news articles
jobs.fire: waiting for the first invoice with the new duty on it

forces.push: a sudden duty can turn a product from profit to loss
forces.pull: the hit per product and the options, with dates
forces.habit: we wait and see
forces.anxiety: what if the rule changes again next week

jobs.little_hire: each time a trade rule changes

watch.metric: added cost per unit from duty changes, by product
watch.source: product origin and duty rates in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 25 percent duty was found on the invoice. After: it is known 5 weeks ahead, price rises 8 percent on 3 products and an order is pulled forward.
jobs.not_for: a store that makes and sells in one country with no imports

jobs.job: When sales dip for a quarter and I cannot tell if it is us or the market, tell me whether our category is growing or shrinking, quarter by quarter against last year, so I know whether to fix us or ride it out
jobs.circumstance: Quarterly review, revenue down 8 percent on last year, the team blames ads, and I suspect the whole category is soft

progress.functional: know category demand this quarter against the same quarter last year
progress.emotional: stop blaming the team, or myself, for a market-wide dip
progress.social: explain the quarter to a partner or investor with the market in view

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, a friend in the industry, or a paid report once a year
jobs.fire: the guess that it is our fault, or the excuse that it is the market

forces.push: fixing the wrong thing wastes a quarter
forces.pull: our trend and the category trend on one line, each quarter
forces.habit: we judge ourselves only against last year
forces.anxiety: what if search data is a poor stand-in for real category sales

jobs.little_hire: every quarter, and when sales move more than 10 percent

watch.metric: category search demand index, this quarter against the same quarter last year
watch.source: public search trend data stored in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: an 8 percent dip was blamed on ads. After: the category is shown down 11 percent, so we held share and kept the ad budget steady.
jobs.not_for: a brand that invented its own category, where there is no market line to compare with yet

jobs.job: When an idea excites me or the team, check it against the basic demand and margin tests in an hour, and help me drop it if it fails, so research time goes to ideas with a chance
jobs.circumstance: Friday, a team member saw a product on TikTok, the founder loves it, and it is about to eat 2 weeks of research

progress.functional: know in an hour if the idea fails a basic check
progress.emotional: let go of a favorite without feeling it was dismissed unfairly
progress.social: say no to a team member's idea with a reason, not a veto

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or 2 weeks of research
jobs.fire: long research on ideas that fail the basics

forces.push: research hours are scarce
forces.pull: a quick pass or fail with the reason
forces.habit: I research what I like
forces.anxiety: what if a quick check kills an idea that would have worked

jobs.little_hire: every time a new idea comes up

watch.metric: ideas stopped at the first check, and research hours saved, per month
watch.source: brand brain idea log

drives.metric: share of funded ideas that pass their margin gate

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 ideas a month get 2 weeks each. After: 2 of the 3 are dropped in an hour, saving about 60 hours a month.
jobs.not_for: a brand with a product team that already runs a strict screen

jobs.job: When a product in my category goes viral on TikTok or Instagram, tell me if it is one clip or real demand across search, marketplaces and other sellers, so I do not chase noise
jobs.circumstance: A 5 million view video, the team asking "should we make one?", and comments full of "where do I buy"

progress.functional: know if the demand shows in 2 or more independent places, and for how long
progress.emotional: stop the fear of missing out on every viral product
progress.social: give the team a clear answer fast

jobs.hire_today: scrolling, a spy tool, or asking a friend

forces.push: viral spikes fade before the stock arrives
forces.pull: one read across search, marketplace sales, ad libraries and other sellers
forces.habit: if it is all over my feed, it must be selling
forces.anxiety: what if I pass and a rival cashes in

jobs.little_hire: whenever a product spikes on social

watch.metric: independent demand sources that agree, and weeks the signal lasts
watch.source: search trends, marketplace ranks and ad libraries in the brand brain

drives.metric: share of first stock order sold within 60 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a viral item was ordered and 40 percent of the stock sat after 90 days. After: only items with 3 sources agreeing get ordered.
jobs.not_for: a brand that never launches trend products

jobs.job: When I am shaping a product or a price, mine the category's reviews for the price buyers call fair and the complaints no one has fixed, so we build and price for what buyers want
jobs.circumstance: Product brief due, 5,000 reviews across rival products, and no time to read them

progress.functional: know the top unfixed complaints and the price range buyers name as fair
progress.emotional: build with confidence that the gap is real
progress.social: brief the supplier and designer with buyer quotes

jobs.hire_today: a freelancer reading reviews, or skimming a few

forces.push: building the same thing as everyone else
forces.pull: a ranked list of complaints and prices, with quotes
forces.habit: we read a few reviews and trust our taste
forces.anxiety: what if the reviews are fake or come from one angry group

jobs.little_hire: before each new product brief or price change

watch.metric: share of category reviews naming the same complaint, and the fair price range buyers state
watch.source: category reviews stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: review rating on our new products, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: new products average 3.9 stars. After: built on the top 3 complaints, new products reach 4.5.
jobs.not_for: a category with too few public reviews to read, such as custom or made-to-order goods

jobs.job: When I set or review a price, tell me which price bands my category buys in and where we sit, so we are not priced out of the band most buyers pick
jobs.circumstance: Pricing a new product, or a price review, with rival prices spread from $10 to $40

progress.functional: know the category's price bands and our price per unit against the middle
progress.emotional: stop second-guessing every price
progress.social: defend the price to the team and to retailers

jobs.hire_today: checking 5 rival sites by hand

forces.push: the wrong band costs volume or margin
forces.pull: price bands with their volume, and our place in them
forces.habit: price near the rival I watch most
forces.anxiety: what if pack sizes make the comparison wrong

jobs.little_hire: at pricing and each quarter

watch.metric: our price per unit against the category's middle price, same pack size
watch.source: rival price capture in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: priced 35 percent above the middle with no premium reason. After: a clear reason on the page, or a price inside the top band.
jobs.not_for: a one-of-a-kind product with no real rivals to compare against

jobs.job: When a new product has been live for 90 days, compare what it really makes with what we planned before launch, so I learn whether my launch math can be trusted
jobs.circumstance: A quarter after launch, sales look okay, and no one has pulled the real margin with ad cost and returns

progress.functional: know actual margin per unit after ad cost and returns, against the plan
progress.emotional: stop fooling myself about a product I championed
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Once a product is live no one goes back to the plan, because it means admitting a miss

forces.push: weak products keep eating ad budget
forces.pull: planned and actual side by side, with the gap explained
forces.habit: a launched product is a done decision
forces.anxiety: what if the product looks worse than it is because launch costs land early

jobs.little_hire: 90 days after each launch

watch.metric: actual margin per unit after ad cost and returns, against planned margin, 90 days after launch
watch.source: Shopify orders, returns and ad spend by product

drives.metric: gross profit from products launched in the last 12 months

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a product planned at $14 a unit makes $3. After: it is seen at day 90, ads are cut and the price is raised.
jobs.not_for: a store that launched nothing in the last year

jobs.job: When I plan stock and cash for the year, map when demand peaks in my category month by month, so money and stock are ready before the rush
jobs.circumstance: Planning next year, last year's sales show peaks, and I do not know which were us and which were the season

progress.functional: know category demand by month over 3 years, against our sales by month
progress.emotional: stop being caught short in the peak
progress.social: give the supplier and team a calendar they can plan to

jobs.hire_today: last year's sales, or gut feel
jobs.fire: last year as the only guide

forces.push: the peak decides the year
forces.pull: a month-by-month demand map
forces.habit: order like last year
forces.anxiety: what if this year's peak moves

jobs.little_hire: at yearly planning and before each season

watch.metric: category demand by month over 3 years, against our sales by month
watch.source: search trend data in the brand brain, Shopify sales

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: stock landed 3 weeks after the peak started. After: it lands 2 weeks before.
jobs.not_for: a category with flat demand all year

jobs.job: When the cost to reach a buyer in my category keeps rising, tell me whether it is our ads or the whole category getting pricier, so I fix the right thing
jobs.circumstance: Cost per 1,000 views up 25 percent, the agency says "the market is expensive", and I cannot check

progress.functional: know ad prices in our category against ours, month by month
progress.emotional: stop wondering if the agency is making excuses
progress.social: hold the agency to a fair standard

jobs.hire_today: the agency's word, or a benchmark blog post
jobs.fire: the agency's excuse as the only view

forces.push: rising ad cost is the biggest input cost for most online stores
forces.pull: our cost next to the category's
forces.habit: accept the agency's reason
forces.anxiety: what if the benchmark is not like our store

jobs.little_hire: monthly

watch.metric: our cost per 1,000 views against the category benchmark, monthly
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, platform benchmarks

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: our cost per 1,000 views is up 30 percent against 10 percent for the category. After: the gap is traced to tired creative and closed in 4 weeks.
jobs.not_for: a store that runs no paid ads

jobs.job: When carriers and the warehouse raise their rates, tell me what it adds per order and which products it hurts most, so I change packs, prices or thresholds before margin slips
jobs.circumstance: A January rate letter from the carrier and the 3PL, 6 percent up, with heavy products hit hardest

progress.functional: know shipping and handling cost per order by product, each quarter
progress.emotional: stop the drip of hidden cost
progress.social: negotiate with the 3PL on facts

jobs.hire_today: the 3PL invoice, or the bookkeeper at year end
jobs.fire: finding it in the invoice months later

forces.push: shipping is a large cost on every order
forces.pull: cost per order by product, with the change shown
forces.habit: pay the invoice
forces.anxiety: what if the split by product is rough

jobs.little_hire: at each rate change and each quarter

watch.metric: shipping and handling cost per order by product, quarter
watch.source: 3PL and carrier invoices, Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: shipping per order rose from $7.40 to $8.60 unnoticed. After: it is seen in week 1, and pack sizes and the free shipping line are changed.
jobs.not_for: a store where buyers pay the full shipping cost at checkout

jobs.job: When our revenue is up and everyone is happy, tell me where we are growing slower than the market, product line by product line, so I see the share we are losing inside the growth
jobs.circumstance: Year end, revenue up 15 percent, and a line or two quietly up only 2 percent while its category grew 20

progress.functional: know our growth minus category growth, by product line, each quarter
progress.emotional: swap false comfort for a clear view
progress.social: show the team where to push next year, with evidence

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Owners compare only to last year, because market numbers are hard to find and growth feels like enough
jobs.fire: growth against last year as the only measure

forces.push: a line that loses share today loses its place in 2 years
forces.pull: each line's gap to its market, in points and dollars
forces.habit: up is good
forces.anxiety: what if the category data is too rough to split by line

jobs.little_hire: every quarter

watch.metric: our revenue growth minus category demand growth, by product line, quarter
watch.source: Shopify sales and search trend data in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the gift line grew 3 percent while its category grew 18 percent, and no one saw it. After: the gap is named, and the line gets a new offer and budget.
jobs.not_for: a one-product store, where the whole business is one line and the category job covers it

jobs.job: When a trend looks hot and a supplier wants a big minimum order, tell me if it is a year-round product, a seasonal one or a fad, and plan cash to match, so I do not buy stock that fades before it sells
jobs.circumstance: Minimum order of 3,000 units, a 12 week lead time, and a demand chart that shot up in the last 2 months

progress.functional: know the demand shape over 3 years and how long cash will be tied up
progress.emotional: stop the fear of a warehouse full of last year's trend
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, a trend tool, or the supplier's word

forces.push: fad stock turns into write-offs
forces.pull: a label for the demand shape, with the months cash is tied up
forces.habit: order big to get the unit price down
forces.anxiety: what if it is a lasting trend and I order too little

jobs.little_hire: before any first order or large reorder

watch.metric: share of stock value in seasonal or fad products, with months of cover
watch.source: inventory in the brand brain, search trends

drives.metric: value of stock older than 180 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $30k of a fad product was sold at half price. After: a small first order, reordered twice as demand held.
jobs.not_for: a brand whose whole range is year-round basics

jobs.job: When a category is growing, tell me if there is still room or it is already full of sellers, so I do not walk into a price war
jobs.circumstance: A promising category, demand up 40 percent, and I do not know how many sellers joined

progress.functional: know demand growth next to the count of active sellers, by quarter
progress.emotional: avoid the regret of joining late
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: a spy tool, marketplace searches, or gut feel

forces.push: crowded categories squeeze margin fast
forces.pull: growth and crowding in one view
forces.habit: growth means go
forces.anxiety: what if seller counts miss the ones selling off the big platforms

jobs.little_hire: before entering a category, then each quarter

watch.metric: category demand growth next to the count of active sellers, quarter
watch.source: search trends, marketplace and ad library counts in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: we entered a category where sellers tripled in a year and price fell 30 percent. After: that category is skipped for one growing with steady seller numbers.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no plan to enter a new category

jobs.job: When margin keeps slipping and I cannot say why, explain in plain words who can squeeze my margin, like suppliers, marketplaces, ad platforms, rivals, cheaper substitutes and new sellers, so I push back on the right one
jobs.circumstance: Gross margin down 4 points in a year, costs up, prices flat, and no clear culprit

progress.functional: know which pressure moved margin, and by how much
progress.emotional: stop feeling squeezed by everything at once
progress.social: explain the margin story to a partner or investor

jobs.hire_today: a consultant once a year, or nothing
jobs.fire: blaming ads or the supplier by default

forces.push: margin pressure grows quietly
forces.pull: each pressure named with its share of the change
forces.habit: we cut costs across the board
forces.anxiety: what if it is too much theory to act on

jobs.little_hire: each quarter, and when margin moves more than 2 points

watch.metric: gross margin per unit, quarter, split by the cost or price change behind it
watch.source: product costs, fees, ad costs and prices in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 4 point drop with no known cause. After: 2.5 points traced to marketplace fees, fixed by moving sales to our own site.
jobs.not_for: a store whose margin is steady and healthy

jobs.job: When sales on our own site flatten, tell me where buyers in my category are moving from and to, like from brand sites to Amazon or TikTok Shop, or from search to AI answers, so we follow the buyer instead of fighting it
jobs.circumstance: Direct sales flat, rivals' marketplace listings growing, and the team debating whether to go on Amazon

progress.functional: know the share of category buying by channel, each quarter
progress.emotional: stop the fear of missing where buyers went
progress.social: make the channel call with the team on facts

jobs.hire_today: a consultant, a marketplace agency's pitch, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the agency pitch as the only view

forces.push: buyers leaving our channel shrink us even when the category grows
forces.pull: channel shares over time, with our share in each
forces.habit: we sell where we always have
forces.anxiety: what if a new channel hurts our margin or brand

jobs.little_hire: each quarter, and before any channel decision

watch.metric: share of category searches and sales by channel, quarter
watch.source: search trends, marketplace ranks and AI referral data in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: direct is flat and rivals' marketplace share rose from 30 to 45 percent. After: a marketplace test is launched, with 20 percent of new sales there in 6 months.
jobs.not_for: a brand bound by retail deals that rule out new channels

jobs.job: When a product line has slid for 2 quarters, tell me whether the product, the market or our ads are to blame before I cut it, so I do not kill a good product for a fixable reason
jobs.circumstance: Sales on a line down 25 percent over 2 quarters, and the team wants to discontinue it

progress.functional: separate market decline from our own ad, page or stock problems
progress.emotional: make a hard call without regret
progress.social: explain the call to the team who built it

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or the agency's view

forces.push: a wrong cut loses a product that could come back
forces.pull: the causes weighed with numbers
forces.habit: falling sales means kill it
forces.anxiety: what if we keep a dying product too long

jobs.little_hire: when a line falls 2 quarters running

watch.metric: product line revenue against its category demand, with ad spend and stockout days beside it, 2 quarters
watch.source: Shopify, ad platforms, search trends

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a line was cut when its category was flat and the drop came from 40 stockout days. After: stock is fixed and sales are back within a quarter.
jobs.not_for: a product that was always a planned one-season run

jobs.job: When our range has grown and half the products barely sell, tell me which to cut and what cash and time it frees, so the team focuses on what sells
jobs.circumstance: 80 products, 20 of them make 85 percent of sales, and the rest tie up stock and photo shoots

progress.functional: know profit, stock value and sales trend for each product
progress.emotional: let go of products without feeling it was a mistake to make them
progress.social: tell the team which products to stop working on

jobs.hire_today: a spreadsheet at stock count, or gut feel

forces.push: slow products tie up cash and attention
forces.pull: a cut list with the cash freed
forces.habit: never discontinue
forces.anxiety: what if a small product brings in buyers who then buy more

jobs.little_hire: twice a year

watch.metric: products with under 1 percent of sales and over 180 days of stock, and their stock value
watch.source: Shopify sales and inventory

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $45k sits in slow products. After: 18 products are cut and $30k freed over 2 quarters.
jobs.not_for: a one-product or few-product store

jobs.job: When our best seller carries most of the business and the team asks "what next?", pick the next product for that line and say why it is different, so we grow without betting everything on one item
jobs.circumstance: Yearly planning, one product is 60 percent of revenue, and 5 ideas are on the table

progress.functional: choose the next product with a named reason to exist and a demand check
progress.emotional: ease the fear that one product failing sinks the business
progress.social: give investors and the team a clear product plan

jobs.hire_today: the founder's instinct, customer requests, or copying a rival's range
jobs.fire: launching colors and sizes because we can

forces.push: the risk of depending on one product
forces.pull: a short list with the reason each would sell to our buyers
forces.habit: add more versions of the hero
forces.anxiety: what if the new product eats sales of the hero

jobs.little_hire: twice a year at product planning

watch.metric: share of revenue from the top product, and next products with a written reason to exist
watch.source: Shopify sales, brand brain

drives.metric: revenue from products other than the top one

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 62 percent of revenue comes from 1 product. After: under 50 percent in 12 months, with 2 launches.
jobs.not_for: a large catalogue store with no single hero product

jobs.job: When a new product is about to launch and creative asks "who is this for and what do we say", hand them the buyer and angle the research found, so launch ads are not a guess
jobs.circumstance: 3 weeks to launch, the agency needs a brief, and the research sits in the founder's head

progress.functional: pass on the buyer, the problem, the proof and the reason for the price in one brief
progress.emotional: trust that the launch money is well aimed
progress.social: give the agency a brief they respect

jobs.hire_today: a call with the agency, a slide, or nothing written down

forces.push: launch ads that miss waste the launch budget
forces.pull: research turned into a brief
forces.habit: tell the agency on a call
forces.anxiety: what if the research angle is wrong and I have locked the agency into it

jobs.little_hire: at every launch

watch.metric: launch ads with a research-backed angle, and their cost per purchase in the first 14 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, brand brain

drives.metric: revenue in the first 60 days of a launch

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 launch angles are guessed and 1 works. After: 2 research angles are tested and 1 wins in week 1.
jobs.not_for: a brand that launches through retail only, with no ads of its own

jobs.job: When a new product needs claims, labels or safety tests, clear the rules before money goes in, so a launch is not pulled or fined after the stock is paid for
jobs.circumstance: A new product with a "non-toxic" claim, sold in 2 countries, with samples coming next month

progress.functional: know the claim, label and test rules for each country before sampling
progress.emotional: stop the fear of a recall or a platform ban
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: an outside lawyer or consultant, or skipping it

forces.push: a pulled product loses the whole stock order
forces.pull: a checklist per product and country, with dates
forces.habit: we copy what rivals say on their labels
forces.anxiety: what if the check misses a rule and I feel safe when I am not

jobs.little_hire: before each new product or new country

watch.metric: new products cleared on claims, labels and tests before sampling
watch.source: brand brain product records

drives.metric: products pulled or fined per year

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 product was delisted by a marketplace for a missing test. After: every new product is cleared before sampling.
jobs.not_for: a store selling plain goods with no claims and no safety rules, where a lawyer's one-off check is enough

jobs.job: When the monthly product meeting comes up, bring a short ranked list of product ideas with a go or no-go note on each, so we decide in the room instead of debating for weeks
jobs.circumstance: Monthly product meeting, 8 ideas raised, and no common way to compare them

progress.functional: rank ideas on the same checks and decide
progress.emotional: end the endless "let's look more" loop
progress.social: make fair calls across the team's ideas

jobs.hire_today: a Notion board, a slide deck, or the founder's pick

forces.push: ideas stall for months
forces.pull: the same checks for every idea, ranked
forces.habit: we discuss until someone gives in
forces.anxiety: what if the ranking favors safe ideas

jobs.little_hire: at the monthly product meeting

watch.metric: ideas decided go or no-go within 30 days of being raised
watch.source: brand brain idea log

drives.metric: products launched per year that pass their margin gate

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: ideas wait 3 months. After: every idea is decided within 30 days.
jobs.not_for: a solo founder with 1 or 2 ideas at a time

jobs.job: When I want the next thing before rivals see it, catch search terms and needs in my category that have grown steadily for 3 months, so we move while it is still cheap to win
jobs.circumstance: Monthly planning, a hunch that buyers want something new, and feeds full of noise

progress.functional: know which terms have grown 3 or more months in a row
progress.emotional: feel ahead instead of behind
progress.social: bring the team a new idea with evidence

jobs.hire_today: Nothing, or scrolling social. Trend tools are noisy and no one has time to sift them
jobs.fire: waiting until a rival launches it

forces.push: late entry costs more to win
forces.pull: a short list of steady risers, not spikes
forces.habit: we react to rivals
forces.anxiety: what if it is a fad that only looks steady

watch.metric: category search terms with 3 or more months of steady growth
watch.source: search trend data in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue from products or pages built on early trends

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: we launched on a trend 9 months after the first rival. After: 3 months ahead, with lower ad cost on the new term.
jobs.not_for: a brand that wants to stay the classic choice and not follow trends

jobs.job: When customers keep asking for something we do not sell, in search, emails or reviews, count it and check it against market demand, so we launch what buyers already ask for
jobs.circumstance: Support gets 20 emails a month asking for a kids size, and site search shows "wide fit" again and again

progress.functional: know the top unmet requests and the market demand behind each
progress.emotional: none
progress.social: show customers we listen

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Requests sit in the helpdesk and site search logs no one reads

forces.push: buyers leave to find it elsewhere
forces.pull: a ranked list of requests with demand behind them
forces.habit: we build what we planned
forces.anxiety: what if the loud few are not the many

jobs.little_hire: monthly and at product planning

watch.metric: top unmet requests from site search and tickets, monthly count
watch.source: site search, helpdesk, reviews

drives.metric: revenue from products launched on request

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 240 searches a month for a size we do not carry. After: the size is added, with $8k a month in new sales.
jobs.not_for: a store too small to have enough searches or tickets to count

jobs.job: When shoppers start trading down to cheaper options or up to premium ones, tell me which way my category is moving on price, so our range and offers follow the buyer
jobs.circumstance: Prices rising, buyers tighter, reviews saying "too pricey", yet rivals' premium lines are also selling

progress.functional: know the share of category sales by price tier, each quarter
progress.emotional: stop guessing whether to cut price or go premium
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or retail news

forces.push: being in the wrong price tier costs share
forces.pull: price tier shares over time
forces.habit: our price is our price
forces.anxiety: what if the data on rival prices and sales is rough

jobs.little_hire: each quarter and before price changes

watch.metric: share of category sales by price tier, quarter
watch.source: marketplace data and rival price capture in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the middle tier shrank from 50 to 38 percent of category sales. After: we add a value pack and a premium line.
jobs.not_for: a luxury brand that will not change price tier whatever the market does

jobs.job: When an investor, lender or retail buyer asks how big our market is and how fast it grows, give me numbers I can defend, so I look like I know my market
jobs.circumstance: A pitch in 2 weeks, and the last deck used a made-up $10 billion number

progress.functional: a market size and growth rate with sources, sized from our own numbers
progress.emotional: stop the unease of quoting numbers I cannot back
progress.social: look credible to people who fund or stock us

jobs.hire_today: a consultant, a paid report, or a number from a blog

forces.push: weak numbers lose the meeting
forces.pull: a sourced size and growth line
forces.habit: copy the number from last year's deck
forces.anxiety: what if the investor knows better numbers

jobs.little_hire: before each pitch or retail meeting

watch.metric: market size and growth with a named source, and buyers needed per year at our order value
watch.source: brand brain, search trends, public category data

drives.metric: cash raised or retail accounts opened

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a slide with an unsourced number. After: a sized market from 3 sources and our own numbers.
jobs.not_for: a founder not raising money or pitching retailers

jobs.job: When I set next year's revenue target, tell me what the market will likely do, so the target is more than last year plus 20 percent
jobs.circumstance: Year-end planning, the team wants a number and the bank wants a forecast

progress.functional: a target built from market growth plus our own share moves
progress.emotional: stop setting goals I do not believe
progress.social: give the team and the bank a number I can defend

jobs.hire_today: last year plus a guess, or an accountant's forecast

forces.push: wrong targets lead to wrong stock orders and hiring
forces.pull: a target with the market part and our part shown
forces.habit: pick a round number
forces.anxiety: what if the market forecast is wrong

jobs.little_hire: once a year and at the mid-year review

watch.metric: forecast against actual revenue by quarter
watch.source: brand brain plan, Shopify

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the target was missed by 25 percent 2 years running. After: within 10 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store under a year old with no history to build on

jobs.job: When I have 20 reports, newsletters and trend emails unread, tell me the 3 market facts that matter to us this quarter, so I stop feeling behind and stop reading what does not matter
jobs.circumstance: An inbox full of trend newsletters, industry reports and podcast notes, and guilt about not reading them

progress.functional: know the few market changes that affect our sales or costs
progress.emotional: drop the guilt of unread reports
progress.social: sound informed with peers and investors

jobs.hire_today: newsletters, podcasts, industry groups, or skimming

forces.push: hours a week of reading that rarely changes a decision
forces.pull: 3 facts tied to our numbers
forces.habit: I read to feel on top of things
forces.anxiety: what if the thing I skip is the one that matters

jobs.little_hire: monthly

watch.metric: market facts acted on per quarter
watch.source: brand brain decision log

drives.metric: share of big decisions made with market context

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 hours a week of reading, rarely acted on. After: 30 minutes a month, with 2 facts acted on each quarter.
jobs.not_for: an owner who enjoys the reading and uses it well

jobs.job: When I compare product ideas, tell me which ones buyers rebuy and how often, so I pick products that earn more than one order
jobs.circumstance: 2 ideas with similar margin; one is a one-time buy, and one wears out in 6 months

progress.functional: know the rebuy rate and cycle for each idea or product
progress.emotional: none
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or the dates on rival reviews
jobs.fire: judging ideas on first-order margin alone

forces.push: one-time products need new buyers forever
forces.pull: rebuy rate shown beside margin
forces.habit: first-order margin is the test
forces.anxiety: what if the rebuy guess for a new product is wrong

jobs.little_hire: at product planning

watch.metric: repeat purchase rate at 90 days by product, and the category's rebuy cycle
watch.source: Shopify orders, reviews in the brand brain

drives.metric: gross profit per customer at 180 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a one-time product was chosen over a rebuy one. After: the rebuy product is picked, and 22 percent of its buyers reorder in 6 months.
jobs.not_for: a brand that sells only one-time items by design, such as furniture

jobs.job: When an idea has been "in research" for weeks, make me decide go, no-go or drop, so research does not quietly eat the team's month
jobs.circumstance: 3 ideas in research since last quarter, each "almost done"

progress.functional: see ideas past their time limit, and force a call
progress.emotional: stop the slow drain of work that never ends
progress.social: give the team closure on their work

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. No one tracks research hours, because each idea always feels close

forces.push: hours go to ideas that never ship
forces.pull: a nudge with the hours spent and what is still missing
forces.habit: one more week
forces.anxiety: what if we drop an idea one step from proof

jobs.little_hire: weekly

watch.metric: ideas past their research time limit
watch.source: brand brain idea log

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 ideas have been in research over 60 days. After: none over 30 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no product research running

jobs.job: When a supplier, agency or guru pitches a product as "selling like crazy", check what they gain and whether the demand is real, so I do not buy on someone else's interest
jobs.circumstance: A supplier's email with a "trending" item and a 1,000 unit minimum

progress.functional: know the source's interest and the real demand evidence
progress.emotional: stop feeling sold to
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or trusting the supplier

forces.push: suppliers push what they want to move
forces.pull: a quick check of the claim
forces.habit: trust the long-time supplier
forces.anxiety: what if I offend a good supplier

jobs.little_hire: whenever someone pitches a product

watch.metric: pitched products checked before order, and their 60 day sell-through
watch.source: brand brain idea log, inventory

drives.metric: value of stock older than 180 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 pitched products were bought last year and both sold slowly. After: both are checked and 1 is declined.
jobs.not_for: a brand that designs every product itself and takes no pitches

jobs.job: When buyers turn out to use our product for something we never planned, size that use as its own market, so we can decide whether to build for it
jobs.circumstance: Reviews show nurses and hikers buy our socks for long shifts and trails, a use we never marketed

progress.functional: know how many buyers have that use and how big that market is
progress.emotional: none
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. The pattern sits in reviews and nobody sizes it

forces.push: missed markets go to rivals
forces.pull: a sized use with buyer count and demand
forces.habit: we market the use we designed for
forces.anxiety: what if it is a small group that is loud in reviews

jobs.little_hire: each quarter

watch.metric: share of reviews and survey answers naming the use, and search demand for it
watch.source: reviews, surveys, search trends in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue from products or pages for the new use

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9 percent of reviews name long work shifts, and it is never used. After: a page and ads for shift workers bring in $12k a month.
jobs.not_for: a brand with a narrow, regulated use it cannot market beyond

jobs.job: When I think about selling in a new country, check the demand and the margin after duties, shipping and local prices before spending, so we do not open a market that loses money
jobs.circumstance: Orders from Canada or the UK trickling in, and a partner suggesting a local store

progress.functional: know margin per unit and category demand in the new country
progress.emotional: move from curiosity to a clear yes or no
progress.social: bring the partner a sized answer

jobs.hire_today: a consultant, a 3PL's pitch, or just trying it
jobs.fire: opening the market to "see what happens"

forces.push: a new market uses cash and team time
forces.pull: a sized case with margin and demand
forces.habit: ship there and see
forces.anxiety: what if the buyer there is different from ours

jobs.little_hire: when orders from a new country pass a set share, or yearly

watch.metric: modelled margin per unit and category demand in the new country
watch.source: orders by country, duty and shipping rates, search trends in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 percent of orders come from abroad and are sold at a loss after shipping. After: 1 country is chosen and priced for duties, with positive margin.
jobs.not_for: a store that ships only in its home country and plans to stay there

jobs.job: When I look for the next product or partner, tell me which nearby categories our buyers also buy are growing, so we grow into them before someone else does
jobs.circumstance: Our sock buyers also buy underwear and slippers, and I do not know if either is growing fast

progress.functional: know the growth of categories our buyers also buy, quarter over quarter
progress.emotional: none
progress.social: pitch partner brands with a reason

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. No one tracks it, because it needs both customer data and market data

forces.push: next-door categories are the cheapest growth
forces.pull: a ranked list of growing nearby categories
forces.habit: we stick to what we sell
forces.anxiety: what if our buyers are only a small group in that category

jobs.little_hire: each quarter and at product planning

watch.metric: growth of categories our buyers also buy, quarter over quarter
watch.source: order data, surveys and search trends in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no view at all. After: 1 growing next-door category found, with 2 products launched there in 12 months.
jobs.not_for: a brand focused on winning its one category first
